title: DEC-240 CI hardening: remaining low and info findings from the OMARK-102 round-1 review (not started)
description: Filed from the Opus round-1 review of opum-ai/opum-marketplace#235 (OMARK-102), relayed by the leader 2026-10-28. All predate that PR and none is started. Relayed wording, not read from the reviewer record. LOW-3: the workflow-hardening rules run per line, not per command, and comments are not stripped, so an npm ci with the flag followed by && npm rebuild passes, and an npm install with the flag only inside a trailing comment passes. LOW-4: layout evasions of the line reader: a run key with two spaces after the dash, a quoted run key, a flow-style mapping, run with an indentation indicator or a trailing comment after the block marker, and *.yaml workflow files skipped by the .yml filter. LOW-5 remainder: extensions.worktreeConfig with a .git/config.worktree file evades --local; url insteadOf rewrites, a token in remote.origin.url and credential.helper are INFO only. LOW-6: a whitespace-only managed block reports no Quest CLI line instead of empty. LOW-2 remainder: npm subcommands the pattern does not list (update, dedupe, audit fix, link, install abbreviations, ic, sit, init, create) and quoted or path-prefixed npm. PROPOSAL, not a decision: a job-level npm_config_ignore_scripts set to true would make the lint a backstop instead of the only control. That is a CI-design change for the leader and opum-doc to decide.

acceptanceCriteria.text: each listed finding is fixed or recorded as declined with a reason
a fixture or mutant proves each fixed finding both ways in the suite itself

implementationNotes: ROUND-2 REVIEW ADDITIONS 2026-10-28, relayed by the leader from the r2 Opus unit; wording is the relay, not the reviewer record. (1) LOW: the whole-line comment strip in assert-main-fast-forward.test.sh (near line 445) hides a real reference inside a YAML block scalar or a run pipe body, for example an AUTH key with a pipe value followed by a hash-prefixed secrets reference. Cheap fix proposed: drop the strip, since the guard job is silent without it, and move that clean fixture into the firing set. (2) LOW: the token scan covers only the guard job slice. A workflow-level env holding a secret is inherited, a join over github.* expression gets through, and so does an expression split across lines. (3) LOW: npm install -g --ignore-scripts false "x" evades the allowlist because nopt reads the next word as the value. (4) INFO: a non-space prefix stuck to the flag (empty quotes or a backslash before --ignore-scripts=false) hides it from the occurrence scan.

OMARK-106 DELIVERED (PR on chore/omark-106-ci-hardening-remainder). FIXED, each proven both ways in the suites (rejecting fixture + accepting fixture, and mutants of the check red on the predicted subset): LOW-3 per-command + comment-stripped npm rule (workflow-hardening.test.mjs); LOW-4 layouts: multi-space dash, quoted run key, block header with indentation indicator/chomping/trailing comment, flow-style refused outright, *.yaml now read; LOW-2 remainder: update/up/upgrade/dedupe/ddp/audit fix/link/ln/init/innit/create, install abbreviations, ic/sit, quoted and path-prefixed npm; LOW-5 config.worktree read by assert-no-persisted-credential.sh; LOW-6 whitespace-only managed block reports empty (read-quest-version.sh); R2-1 whole-line comment strip dropped from the token scan; R2-2 token scan now reads the whole promotion-guards.yml plus github.*, bare github handed to a function, and a split-across-lines expression; R2-3 bare --ignore-scripts followed by true/false/null/number refused; R2-4 a token with a stuck prefix is not the bare flag and is refused.

DECLINED, with reasons: LOW-5 INFO items (url insteadOf rewrites, a token in remote.origin.url, credential.helper) - INFO only in the review and none is the actions/checkout persistence mechanism this check measures; npm run/test/start/pack/publish/version not treated as risky - they run the root package own scripts, not a dependency lifecycle script, and listing them would flag every legitimate script call. OPEN: AC 3, the npm_config_ignore_scripts job-level proposal, is a CI-design decision for the leader and opum-doc and is NOT decided here; task stays In Progress until that answer is recorded.

ROUND-1 REVIEW OF #243 (Opus, 8bf321d): B1 (comment strip hid a whole command) and B2 (lookahead missed subshell/$()/backtick/redirect forms) fixed with rejecting fixtures, each confirmed to fail on 8bf321d. Nit 4 taken (npm run/test accepted; npm run ci is a script named ci), nit 5 taken (unparseable config.worktree fails closed), nit 6 taken (depth_raw renamed wf_raw). KNOWN, not fixed: nit 3 - flow-style refusal does not cover a quoted run key inside a flow list, or a flow list whose bracket opens on its own line; nit 7 (pre-existing) - a dash-only step line, a run value continued onto the next line, a folded run > block splitting npm and ci, run: &anchor |, and --ignore-scripts $VAR are not read. These lexical evasions are what the npm_config_ignore_scripts proposal (AC 3) would make moot.

ROUND-2 REVIEW OF #243 (Opus, 9b099f3): blockers 1-5 fixed (flag value read as subcommand; nested npm after a safe first word; quote-unaware split dropping a piece or forging a bare flag, now a quote-aware splitter and comment cut; following-word boundary), nit 6 (unmatched-only strip of a trailing ) or backtick) and nit 8 (npm run ci && npm ci pinned) taken, each rejecting fixture confirmed NOT rejected on 9b099f3 (R2-8 already was; it is pinned). KNOWN, not fixed: nit 7 - the recorded reason for leaving pack/publish out ("root package lifecycle only") is UNVERIFIED (npm pack of a git spec may prepare a git dependency); they are not on the risky list. Third round of lexical leaks in one line reader: AC 3 (job-level npm_config_ignore_scripts) has gone to opum-doc.

RULING opum-doc 2026-11-17 (option A), relayed by the leader, after three Opus review rounds on #243 each found the line scanner trading old evasions for new ones (round 3: comment-cut misreads, quote-unaware paren and backtick strip, multi-line blocks, continuation joins). LOW-2 and LOW-3 are SUPERSEDED by OMARK-109 (job-level npm_config_ignore_scripts); AC 3 moved there. The #243 scanner (commands(), npmRisk, comment strip, safe-word allowlist, paren strip) is REMOVED and dev NPM_CMD line rule restored unchanged as the backstop. Kept, additive: LOW-4 layouts, LOW-5 config.worktree, LOW-6, R2 token scan, --ignore-scripts value checks (R2-3, R2-4). Round 4 is a no-regression check against dev only.

ROUND-4 REVIEW OF #243 (Opus, 25d16b2): blocker fixed (the quoted/spaced run key is read only on the step dash line or at the step key column; dev unquoted any-depth match kept; R4-a/b/c rejecting fixtures, each confirmed accepted on 25d16b2); nits 4, 5 (correction on OMARK-109) and 6 taken. KNOWN, not fixed: nit 2 - the step-start regex requires a colon after the key, so `- name-x:` (not a valid step key) is read by dev as a step and not here; nit 3 - a `- run:` line inside a block scalar under the checkout with: is read as the next step (dev does the same), and the header `run: | # npm install x` is now a block header rather than a one-line value (it is a YAML comment and never executes).

VERDICT ROUND 1 on #243 (Opus review unit; verbatim from verdict-opum-marketplace-review-243.txt):
VERDICT: REQUEST CHANGES
Review of opum-ai/opum-marketplace#243 at 8bf321d0f2e1fbe9c47f5adfc3ccb01d6374bdf8 (OMARK-106). Model: claude-opus-5-5.

The brief's bar is that no guard is weakened and the PR adds no new way to evade the scan. Findings 1 and 2 each reopen an npm evasion that the OLD per-line rule caught. I found both by tracing the regexes by hand; I could not run them.

FINDINGS

1. BLOCKING — scripts/test/workflow-hardening.test.mjs:73 and :75: the comment strip can hide a whole npm command.
   - The pattern `(^|\s)#.*$` does not know about quotes, and `commands()` strips before it splits.
   - So `echo " #" && npm ci`, `FOO=" #" npm ci` and `echo "step #1"; npm install x` all lose everything after the space-hash. `npmRisk` then sees no npm, and no violation is reported. Bash still runs the npm command.
   - The old code ran `NPM_CMD` on the raw line and flagged all three.
   - The comment at :70-72 says the strip "can only drop a flag and so can only over-report, never hide a violation". That is false: it can drop the command itself.
   - Fix direction: judge risk on the unstripped command and look for the flag only in the stripped one, i.e. `npmRisk(raw) && !hasIgnoreScripts(stripped)`, or make the strip quote-aware.
   - I checked ci.yml: no shell comment inside a run body mentions npm, so the first option would not add false positives on the real files today.
   - Add the three lines above as rejecting fixtures.

2. BLOCKING — scripts/test/workflow-hardening.test.mjs:87 (and `NPM_TOKEN` at :79): the new `(?=\s|$)` lookahead is stricter than the old `\b`.
   - `(cd sub && npm ci)` splits into the piece `npm ci)`. `ci` is followed by `)`, so `NPM_SUB` fails and nothing is flagged.
   - The same happens with `$(npm ci)`, a backticked npm ci, and `npm ci>/dev/null`.
   - `NPM_TOKEN` has the same problem: `$(which npm) ci` fails because `npm` is followed by `)`.
   - The old `NPM_CMD` matched all of these. `(cd dir && npm ci)` is a common idiom.
   - Fix: let both lookaheads also stop at `)`, `>`, `<` and the backtick, and add rejecting fixtures for each form.

3. NIT — scripts/test/workflow-hardening.test.mjs:120: the flow-style refusal does not cover every flow layout.
   - The third pattern `\brun\s*:` misses a quoted key: `steps:` with `[ { "run": "npm ci" } ]` on the next line passes.
   - So does a flow sequence or mapping whose `[`/`{` opens on a line of its own: `steps:` / `[` / `{` / `run: npm ci }` / `]`.
   - Neither layout is read as a step, so neither is scanned.
   - This is not a regression, but the claim that flow style is "refused outright" is only partly true.

4. NIT — scripts/test/workflow-hardening.test.mjs:87 and :269-279: the declined subcommands (run, test and so on) have no accepting fixture.
   - Because `NPM_SUB` scans the whole rest of the command, `npm run ci` and `npm test -- x` are flagged (`ci` and `x` are on the list). That over-reports, so it weakens nothing.
   - But it does not match the recorded decline, and nothing in the suite pins the intended behaviour. Add an accept for `npm run build` and decide what `npm run ci` should do.

5. NIT — scripts/ci/assert-no-persisted-credential.sh:48-51: the new "could not read config.worktree" branch fails closed, but no fixture exercises it. A malformed config.worktree would. Also :57, the success line counts only `--local` keys; it could report that config.worktree was also read.

6. NIT — scripts/test/assert-main-fast-forward.test.sh:443-445.
   - With `-i`, `github[[:space:]]*[,)]` now fires on prose anywhere in the file, such as "(see GitHub)" in a comment. That is brittle (over-report only), not a weakening.
   - The name `depth_raw` now holds the whole file, not the job slice; rename it.

7. NIT — pre-existing gaps, not from this diff and not blocking:
   - A dash-only `-` line with the step keys on the lines below is never read as a step (:31).
   - A plain or quoted run value that continues onto the next line, and a folded `run: >` block that splits `npm` and `ci` across lines, are read line by line.
   - `run: &anchor |` is read as a one-line value, so its body is skipped.
   - `--ignore-scripts $VAR` accepts whatever the variable holds.

WHAT I VERIFIED FROM THE DIFF AND THE TREE
- Pins untouched: the diff has exactly 7 files (.quest/tasks/OMARK-106.json, scripts/ci/assert-no-persisted-credential.sh, scripts/ci/read-quest-version.sh and four scripts/test files). Neither .claude-plugin/marketplace.json nor scripts/federated-pin-baselines.json is touched.
- Tightened, not weakened (apart from findings 1 and 2):
  - `hasIgnoreScripts` (:104-114) now reads whole tokens per command. It refuses a prefix stuck to the flag and refuses true/false/null/number after a bare flag; nopt itself consumes only true/false, so refusing more only over-reports.
  - `--no-ignore-scripts` and `=false` are still refused.
  - The `steps()` key regex (:31) and the `runText` header regex (:47, :54) accept a superset of the old layouts.
  - `.yaml` files are now read (:123, :172).
  - read-quest-version.sh:43 treats a whitespace-only block as empty.
  - The credential script now also reads `config.worktree` through `git rev-parse --git-path`, which is correct for linked worktrees. Under `set -euo pipefail` it fails closed, and exit 1 from `--get-regexp` is handled correctly.
  - The token scan reads the whole workflow file with no comment strip, so it can see strictly more than before. TOKEN_RE only gained alternatives.
  - The positive greps that rely on the job slice and the comment strip (:410-423, :491) are unchanged, which is correct: the whole-file warning at :401-409 applies to positive checks, not negative ones.
- Rejecting AND accepting fixtures exist for LOW-3, LOW-4 (multi-space dash, quoted key, |2, | # note), LOW-2 (plus accepts for `npm audit`, update with the flag and path-prefixed npm), LOW-5 (wtcfg/wtclean), LOW-6 (the live CLAUDE.md is the accepting control), R2-1, R2-2, R2-3 and R2-4.
  - Flow style and `>-` have rejecting fixtures only, which is acceptable for a refusal.
- Pass floors: 38 to 76 (26 new rejects + 12 new accepts), 12 to 15, and 21 to 23. Each matches the cases added.
- By reading it, promotion-guards.yml has no line matching the widened TOKEN_RE, so the whole-file scan should return 1 on it.
- AC 3: nothing in the diff depends on a job-level npm_config_ignore_scripts, and nothing references it. Observation only, not counted against the PR: the evasions left over are lexical (`n\pm`, `"n"pm`, `$NPM`, folded scalars). A line linter cannot close them; a job-level setting would make them moot.

WHAT A TREE READ COULD NOT ESTABLISH
- That the three suites pass at this head, including that the real promotion-guards.yml gives rc=1 now that the strip is gone, and that ci.yml still counts installs === 2.
- The writer's mutant runs claimed in the OMARK-106 notes.
- That my traces of findings 1 and 2 hold when executed; they are hand traces of the regexes.
- Whether npm's option parser expands an abbreviated long option such as `--ignore-script=false`. If it does, that is a pre-existing hole the flag regex never matched.
- CI status on this SHA.

VERDICT ROUND 2 on #243 (Opus review unit; verbatim from verdict-opum-marketplace-review-243r2.txt):
VERDICT: REQUEST CHANGES
opum-ai/opum-marketplace#243 at 9b099f3be88eca60f33a47923f36bd58c1b96e61 (OMARK-106), round-2 reviewer unit. I read the code but could not run it. Every result below comes from reading the regexes against the input string, and I give each string so the writer can confirm it.

FINDINGS
1. BLOCKING. scripts/test/workflow-hardening.test.mjs:104-105. The new allowlist reads a flag's value as the subcommand.
   - `npm --prefix test ci` passes. The first non-flag word is `test`, which is the value of `--prefix`, so npmRisk returns false. `npm -w test ci` and `npm -C bin install` pass the same way.
   - The dev rule (NPM_CMD, `npm\b[^;&|\n]*?\s(ci|install...)`) caught all three, and so did 8bf321d, so this is a regression.
   - The comment at :96-97 says a flag ahead of the subcommand can only over-report. It can also hide a command.
   - Fix: apply the safe-word shortcut only when the safe word comes straight after the npm token, with no flag in between.

2. BLOCKING. workflow-hardening.test.mjs:100-106. Once the first word is safe, nothing after it is checked, including a nested npm.
   - `npm test $(npm install x)` passes. So does npm run build followed by a backticked npm ci.
   - commands() does not split at $( or a backtick, and NPM_TOKEN looks at the first npm only. When that npm's first word is safe, npmRisk returns false.
   - Dev caught `npm test $(npm install x)`. The same miss happens when the first npm is not a command at all: `echo npm test $(npm ci)`.
   - Fix: judge every NPM_TOKEN match in the piece (matchAll), and call it risky if any match is.

3. BLOCKING. workflow-hardening.test.mjs:79. The B1 fix closes the forms the writer named, not the class.
   - `x="|#" npm ci` passes, and so does `FOO="&#" npm ci`. The shell runs npm ci in both.
   - The quote-unaware split at :78 cuts the line at the quoted | or &, which leaves the piece `#" npm ci`. stripComment matches `^#` on that piece, so its flagText is '' and the filter drops it without ever looking at `raw`.
   - 8bf321d caught this because it stripped per line, and the # there follows `|`, not whitespace. Dev caught it too, so the B1 fix itself introduced the regression.
   - Fix: filter on raw, or strip only whole-line comments before the split, and never drop a piece once it is split.

4. BLOCKING. workflow-hardening.test.mjs:78 with :124. The quote-unaware split can make a token that is not the bare flag look bare. This has been present since 8bf321d, so round 1 missed it.
   - `npm ci "--ignore-scripts;"` passes. So do `"--ignore-scripts|x"` and `'--ignore-scripts&'`.
   - The split cuts the token to `"--ignore-scripts`. The quote strip then leaves exactly `--ignore-scripts`.
   - Dev rejected this, because its token was `--ignore-scripts;`. Whatever nopt does with that key, the result breaks the checker's own rule: every occurrence must be exactly the bare flag or =true.

5. BLOCKING (round 1 missed it; the delta makes one form reachable). workflow-hardening.test.mjs:127. The R2-3 check for a following true/false word still ends a word only at whitespace, `(?=\s|$)`. It never got the B2 boundary set.
   - `npm ci --ignore-scripts false>/dev/null` passes. So does `(npm ci --ignore-scripts false)`.
   - nopt reads that false as the value of the boolean flag, so the scripts run.
   - The task notes list R2-3 as FIXED. The paren form became reachable only because of this delta's NPM_TOKEN/NPM_SUB boundary change.
   - Fix: use `(?=[\s)<>`;&|]|$)` here.

6. NIT. workflow-hardening.test.mjs:124. The lead asked whether stripping ) or a backtick can make a non-compliant command look compliant. It can.
   - `npm ci $(: --ignore-scripts)` now passes, and so does `npm ci` followed by a backticked `: --ignore-scripts`. The substitution expands to nothing, so npm ci runs with its scripts.
   - Dev and 8bf321d both rejected these, because the token was `--ignore-scripts)`.
   - It is a NIT rather than a blocker because the class was already on dev: `npm ci $(: --ignore-scripts )`, with a space before the ), passed there. The strip only adds a spelling. It belongs with nit 7's `--ignore-scripts $VAR`.

7. NIT. workflow-hardening.test.mjs:90-92 and :98. The recorded reason for declining `pack` and `publish` ("root package's lifecycle only") may be wrong. `npm pack <git-spec>` has pacote prepare a git dependency, which can run that dependency's prepare script. I did not verify this, see below.

8. NIT. workflow-hardening.test.mjs:299-304. The allowlist has accepting cases but no rejecting case that pins it. Add these as rejecting fixtures: `npm run ci && npm ci` (passes today, worth pinning), plus every string in findings 1-5. Confirm each one fails on 9b099f3 before fixing it.

VERIFIED (by reading the code)
- B1 forms in the fixtures are closed: `echo " #" && npm ci`, `FOO=" #" npm ci` and `echo "step #1"; npm install x`.
- B2 forms are closed: `(cd sub && npm ci)`, `x=$(npm ci)`, a backticked npm ci, `npm ci>/dev/null` and `$(which npm) ci`. For `$(which npm) ci`, rest=`) ci` and the first word is ci.
- Allowlist cases the lead named:
  - `npm run ci && npm ci` is flagged, because the && split leaves a bare npm ci.
  - `npm test; npm install` is flagged.
  - `npm --prefix x ci` is flagged, but only because x is not a safe word (finding 1).
  - `npm run -- ci` is accepted correctly: it runs a root script named ci.
  - `npm -- ci` is flagged.
  - npx is always flagged, and exec/x are in NPM_SUB.
- Everything round 1 verified as tightened is still tightened: all the earlier rejecting fixtures (LOW-2/3/4, R2-3, R2-4, OMARK-102 2-4) are still in `bad`.
- Nit 5: assert-no-persisted-credential.sh:48-50 fails closed. A malformed config.worktree makes git config exit non-1, and the script exits 1. The new test checks for exit 1 and the absence of the clean message.
- Nit 6: the depth_raw to wf_raw rename is complete in that block.
- The pass floor of 88 equals 5 positive controls + 58 bad + 2 good + 18 goodflag + 4 layout + 1 filter. The per-workflow-file oks are slack on top of that.

NOT ESTABLISHED BY A TREE READ
- None of the strings above was executed.
- I did not check what nopt does with an `ignore-scripts;` key, or that `--prefix`, `-w` and `-C` consume the next word (I believe they take a string value).
- I did not check whether `npm pack` of a git spec runs prepare, or whether --ignore-scripts suppresses it.
- I did not check the CI status of 9b099f3.

FRAMING: this is the third round of lexical leaks in the same checker. That is the case for settling AC 3, a job-level npm_config_ignore_scripts=true, and keeping this lint as a backstop.

VERDICT ROUND 3 on #243 (Opus review unit; verbatim from verdict-opum-marketplace-review-243r3.txt):
VERDICT: REQUEST CHANGES
Round-3 review of opum-ai/opum-marketplace#243 at 8a13a6fde76dc6e8dd289bea2a3f41868292c8b5 (OMARK-106). All six round-2 strings are now rejected. The new scanner introduces two classes of miss that dev caught.

Dev's rule judged whole lines, never stripped a comment, and never stripped a trailing `)`. Every BLOCKING input below makes dev's NPM_CMD match with no flag on the line, so dev reports a violation. 8a13a6f accepts each one. The file is scripts/test/workflow-hardening.test.mjs.

FINDINGS

Class A: the comment cut at :91 drops text that bash runs. `commands()` decides that `#` starts a comment by looking back one character. Its quote model is narrower than bash's. Everything after a false comment start is discarded, so the npm in it is never judged.

1. BLOCKING :91, escaped space. Input: `echo x\ #; npm ci`
   - :89 skips the escaped space, then :91 sees `ln[i-1]` as whitespace and cuts.
   - In bash, `#` in the middle of a word is literal, so `npm ci` runs.
2. BLOCKING :91, `#` inside `${...}`. Input: `echo ${x:- #}; npm ci`
3. BLOCKING :91, nested quotes inside `"$( )"`. Input: `x="$(echo " #")"; npm ci`
   - The scanner closes the outer quote at the inner `"`, so it reads ` #` as unquoted.
   - Nested quotes in `"$(...)"` are idiomatic shell.
4. BLOCKING :91, `#` inside backticks. Input: `` echo `true #`; npm ci ``
5. BLOCKING :91, ANSI-C quoting. Input: `echo $'a\' #' && npm ci`
   - Inside `$'...'`, the sequence `\'` is an escaped quote, so bash's string is `a' #`.
   - The scanner closes the quote at `\'` and cuts at ` #`.
6. BLOCKING :91, quote state resets on every line of a `run: |` block. Two-line body:
   - line 1: `echo "`
   - line 2: ` #"; npm ci`
   - Line 2 starts outside quotes for the scanner, so it cuts at ` #`. Bash is still inside the string.
7. BLOCKING :65 with :91, `joinContinuations` (pre-existing) combined with the new cut.
   - (a) Two-line body `# note \` then `npm ci`. Bash never continues a comment, so `npm ci` runs. The joiner produces `# note  npm ci`, and the scanner cuts all of it.
   - (b) Two-line body `echo a\` then `#; npm ci`. Bash sees `echo a#; npm ci`. The joiner inserts a space, producing `echo a #; npm ci`, which is cut.
   - (c) Contrived variant: an unquoted here-doc `bash <<EOF` whose body line is `echo \\\" #"; npm ci`. The outer shell rewrites `\\` to `\`, the inner bash runs `npm ci`, and the scanner cuts.

Class B: the unmatched-`)` and backtick strip (:160-162) counts characters per split piece and ignores quotes. On dev the token `--ignore-scripts)` was never the bare flag.

8. BLOCKING :160-162. Each of these inputs is accepted, and `npm ci` runs with no flag:
   - `( cd x; npm ci $(: --ignore-scripts) )` is valid shell with no escaping. The `;` split moves the subshell's `(` into the other piece, so the counts are `)`=2 and `(`=1. The strip fires and the token reads as the bare flag.
   - `X=")" npm ci $(: --ignore-scripts)` gets through the same way.
   - `npm ci $(: \) --ignore-scripts)` gets through the same way.
   - `` X='`' npm ci `: --ignore-scripts` `` gets through because the backtick count is odd.
   - This reopens round-2 nit 6 in a form dev rejected.

Shared with dev, so NIT:

9. NIT :81-102, ANSI-C desync merging pieces or hiding a comment.
   - `X=$'\'' npm ci # --ignore-scripts`: the scanner sees an unterminated quote, so it never cuts, and the flag in the comment counts.
   - `echo $'\'' ; npm ci ; npm rebuild --ignore-scripts`: the pieces merge.
10. NIT :91, a comment that starts right after an operator. Input: `(npm ci)# --ignore-scripts`
11. NIT :81-102, a quote opened on the previous line merges pieces. Two-line body:
    - line 1: `x="`
    - line 2: `"; npm ci; echo --ignore-scripts`
12. NIT :152-166, the flag is present but has no effect.
    - `npm ci -- --ignore-scripts`: after `--`, the flag is a positional.
    - `npx some-tool --ignore-scripts`: the flag goes to the tool.
    - `npm ci " --ignore-scripts"`: the word starts with a space.
    - `--ignore-script=false`: nopt abbreviation. Unverified for the npm version CI runs.
13. NIT :108 and :116, obfuscated npm names and missing aliases.
    - Not caught: `\npm ci`, `n\pm ci`, `"n"pm ci`, `node /usr/lib/node_modules/npm/bin/npm-cli.js ci`, `npm \ci`, `npm c"i"`.
    - Aliases missing from NPM_SUB: `isnt`, `isnta`, `isntal` (install) and `clean-install-test`.
    - npm prefix abbreviations such as `reb`, `upd`, `dedu` and `exe`: unverified for the npm version CI runs.
14. NIT :166, a new false positive, not an evasion. `npm ci --ignore-scripts 2>/dev/null` and `npm ci --ignore-scripts 2>&1` are now rejected.
    - The round-3 boundary added `<` and `>`, so the fd number reads as the flag's value.
    - Dev and 9b099f3 both accepted these.

Suggested fix, in one line:
- Treat `#` as a piece separator, not a terminator, so the comment text becomes its own piece. Its npm is still judged, but its flag never credits the command before it. That restores dev's behaviour for every Class A input.
- Run the comment handling before `joinContinuations`, or join with an empty string instead of a space.
- Do the paren and backtick matching inside the quote-aware scanner instead of counting characters in a piece.
- Add each BLOCKING string as a rejecting fixture.

PROBE LIST (dev / now)
- Escaped quote: caught / caught. Double-quote and outside-quote backslash handling matches bash on where a quote ends.
- ANSI-C `$'...'`: caught / NEWLY MISSED (finding 5). The comment-hiding form is shared (finding 9).
- Here-doc: caught / caught per body line. It over-reports data lines. Missed only through the escape layer in 7c.
